title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE LAST STORE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Jo Whitaker, the town clerk of Barnet, Vermont.
One cold morning, the only store in town put up a sign. For Sale.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: SOMEBODY SHOULD
segments.quote: Heaven never helps the man who will not act.
segments.author: Sophocles
lines: Hank Dutton's family had run that store for ninety years. Now Hank was tired.
At the town meeting, everybody said, somebody should do something. Then everybody went home.
Jo's dad kept a line from Sophocles taped inside his tractor:
Heaven never helps the man who will not act.
So Jo stood up and said, Fine. Somebody is me.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PRICE
segments.quote: The good we secure for ourselves is precarious and uncertain until it is secured for all of us and incorporated into our common life.
segments.author: Jane Addams
lines: Hank wanted three hundred thousand dollars. Jo had a pickup.
Then she read Jane Addams, who opened a famous neighborhood house in Chicago:
The good we secure for ourselves is precarious and uncertain until it is secured for all of us and incorporated into our common life.
So the whole town would buy the store together. Two hundred dollars a share.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE DOORS
segments.quote: Who is wise? He that learns from every one.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: Jo knocked on doors with a ten-minute speech. Doors closed fast. One goat ate her pen.
Then she remembered Ben Franklin:
Who is wise? He that learns from every one.
So she stopped talking and started asking. What do you miss? Good coffee. A place to sit.
The shares started selling.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: MUD SEASON
segments.quote: It is not in the still calm of life, or the repose of a pacific station, that great characters are formed.
segments.author: Abigail Adams
lines: In March, the old cooler died, and mud season swallowed the delivery truck to its hubcaps.
Her friend Gus, a dairy farmer, read her a letter Abigail Adams wrote her son:
It is not in the still calm of life, or the repose of a pacific station, that great characters are formed.
So Jo rolled up her sleeves. Gus loaned his milk cooler and his tractor.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: TWENTY GRAND SHORT
segments.quote: It is always darkest just before the day dawneth.
segments.author: Thomas Fuller
lines: Three days before the deadline, they were twenty thousand dollars short.
At midnight, Jo stared at her mom's old sampler, from the English writer Thomas Fuller:
It is always darkest just before the day dawneth.
At six a.m., Gus called. The fire department was throwing a pancake breakfast.
Four hundred neighbors came hungry. They made it, with eleven dollars to spare.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: OPENING DAY
segments.quote: The ornament of a house is the friends who frequent it.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: On opening day, the bell over the door rang and rang.
Farmers argued about the weather. Hank gave free advice.
Jo hung a sign by the register, from Ralph Waldo Emerson:
The ornament of a house is the friends who frequent it.
The store still sells milk. Mostly, it sells a place to belong.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Act. Do it together. Ask and learn. Grow in the storm. Hold on till dawn. Keep the door open.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Don't wait for somebody. Do it together. Ask. Grow in the storm. Hold on. Keep the door open.
I bought one share. I mostly use it for free coffee.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
